questions.question: What is the value of [(1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + ……..20)/7]?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

[(1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + ……..20)/7]

**Formula:**

Sum of first n natural number = n (n + 1)

**Calculation:**

Sum of first 20 natural number = (20 × 21)/2 = 210

Now, [(1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + ……..20)/7]

⇒ 210/7

⇒ 30

questions.question: Which of the following fraction is greater than 2/3?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

The given fraction = 2/3

**Calculation:**

Compare on 1/2, 3/7, 4/7 and 6/7

(2/3) × (14/14) = 28/42

(1/2) × (21/21) = 21/42

(3/7) × (6/6) = 18/42

(6/7) × (6/6) = 36/42

Now, we can say

6/7 is greater than 2/3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6bd67c9563cdde4a0dfe99b7686282bc07365f691adfb64c907de66aebe4b011.png] 

2/3 = 1/2 

⇒ 4 = 3 here 4 > 3 therefore 2/3 > 1/2

2/3 = 3/7 

⇒ 14 = 9 here 14 > 9 therefore 2/3 = 3/7 

2/3 = 4/7 

⇒ 14 = 12 here 14 > 12 9 therefore 2/3 > 4/7

2/3 = 6/7 

⇒ 14 = 18 here 14 < 18 therefore 2/3 < 6/7

∴ 6/7 is greater than 2/3.

questions.question: What is the smallest four-digit number which when divided by 2, 3, 4 and 6 leaves remainder 1 in each case?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

The given numbers are 2, 3, 4 and 6.

**Concept:**

The smallest four-digit number is 1000.

**Calculation:**

LCM of 2, 3, 4 and 6 = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12

When we divide 1000 by 12 we get 4 as the remainder.

The smallest four-digit number which is divisible by 2, 3, 4 and 6 is = 1000 – 4 + 12 = 1008

The smallest four-digit number which when divided by 2, 3, 4 and 6 leaves remainder 1 in each case = 1008 + 1 = 1009

**∴ The number will be 1009.**

If a number A is 30% less than another number B and B is 20% more than 150, then what is the value of A?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

A is less than B by = 30%

B is more than 150 by = 20%

**Formula:**

If a number increased by x%, then

Increased number = Actual number × (100 + x)/100

**Calculation:**

B = 150 × 120/100

⇒ B = 180

A = 180 × 70/100

⇒ A = 126

questions.question: If a = (5/4)b and b = (2/10)c, then what is a : b : c?
questions.solution:

a = (5/4)b

b = (2/10)c

**Calculation:**

a = (5/4)b

a : b = 5 : 4

b = (2/10)c

b : c = 2 : 10 ---- (1)

Multiply by 2 in equation (1)

questions.question: If 40 chairs are bought for Rs. 10000, then how many chairs must be sold for 10000 to gain 60%?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

Cost of 40 chairs = Rs. 10000

**Formula:**

SP = CP × (100 + profit)/100

**Calculation:**

Cost of 1 chair = 10000/40 = Rs. 250

Selling price of 1 chair = 250 × 160/100 = Rs. 400

∴ Number of chairs sold for 10000 = 10000/400 = 25

questions.question: Piyush marks the price of his article 30% more than its cost price. If he sells the article for Rs. 780 after following a discount of 20%, then what will be the cost price (in Rs) of the article?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

Piyush marks the price more than the cost price by = 30%

Discount = 20%

Selling price of the article = Rs. 780

**Formula:**

SP = MP × [(100 – Discount%)/100]

**Calculation:**

MP of the article = 780 × 100/80

∴ Cost price of the article = 780 × 100/80 × 100/130 = Rs. 750

questions.question: F and M together can do a piece of work in 8 days. F alone can do the same work in 12 days. In how many days can M alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Days for M alone = (Product of days) ÷ (Difference of days)

Required time = (12 × 8) ÷ (12 − 8)

Required time = 96 ÷ 4 = 24 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time taken by F and M = 8 days; Time taken by F = 12 days.

Formula Used: Total Work = LCM of individual time; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 F + M
 8
 24
 3
 
 

 F
 12
 2
 
 

⇒ Total work assumed (LCM of 8 and 12) = 24 units

⇒ Efficiency of (F + M) = 3 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of F = 2 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of M = (Efficiency of F + M) − (Efficiency of F) = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Time taken by M = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of M = 24 ÷ 1 = 24 days

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Combined Work Formula

If A can complete work in x days and B in y days, then together they finish in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Work-Efficiency Relation

Work = Efficiency × Time. For constant work, efficiency is inversely proportional to time.

Alternate Day Work

For work done on alternate days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days) and divide total work by cycle efficiency.</p
